messages.subject: Striped bars in histogram/bar plot
parts:
Dear all,

I have issues with a simple histogram. I'm plotting a count variable (cfc) as a function of destination (dstroi) and condition (cond). The output in Quartz looks fine, but whenever I save the plot (pdf, cairo_pdf, ggsave, it doesn't matter), it looks weird. Here's two examples:

http://dl.dropbox.com/u/6281903/good.png
http://dl.dropbox.com/u/6281903/badandugly.pdf

And here's the code:

ggplot(subset(imca.CRI, srcroi%in%c(5:8) & dstroi%in%c(1:7))) +
geom_histogram(stat="identity", aes(x=dstroi, y=cfc, fill=cond)) +
xlab("Zielwort") + ylab("Anzahl Fixationen") +
facet_wrap(~cond) + theme_pm() + opts(legend.position="none") +
scale_fill_manual(values=c("#73d216","#cc0000")) +
scale_x_continuous(breaks=1:7,
labels=c("A","verb-te","B","weil","er","Pr+1","Pr+2"))

ggsave(file="cri.pdf", width=7, height=3.5)


I excluded everything unnecessary and the problem persists. The data frame is quite large with 1 380 000 rows, but I tried to plot a subset from only five subjects and that yielded the same result. Finally, I tried geom_bar and geom_histogram, it doesn't make a difference. Does anybody have an idea how to solve this?

Best,
Paul

messages.subject: Re: Striped bars in histogram/bar plot
parts:
Hi:

This works on my system:

df <- data.frame(gp = factor(rep(c('Kongruent', 'Inkongruent'), each = 1000)),
                 Zielwort = sample(c('A', 'verb-te', 'B', 'weil', 'er', 'Pr+1', 'Pr+2'),
                               2000, replace = TRUE,
                               prob = c(0.05, 0.075, 0.075, rep(0.2, 4))))
df$Zielwort <- factor(df$Zielwort, levels = c('A', 'verb-te', 'B', 'weil', 'er', 'Pr+1', 'Pr+2'))
df$gp <- factor(df$gp, levels = c('Kongruent', 'Inkongruent'))
g <- ggplot(df, aes(x = Zielwort))
g + geom_bar(aes(fill = gp)) + facet_wrap(~ gp, nrow = 1) + theme_bw() +
    scale_fill_manual(breaks = levels(df$gp), values = c('green','red')) +
    opts(legend.position = 'none') + opts(panel.border = theme_blank()) +
    opts(axis.ticks = theme_blank()) + ylab('Anzahl Fixationen')
ggsave('zeilbars.pdf', height = 5, width = 7)

(BTW, this is a bar chart, not a histogram - your Zielwort values are categorical, not numeric. Replaying this by summarizing df into a frequency table for Zielwort by each level of gp,

ddfrq <- ddply(df, .(gp), summarise, freq = tabulate(Zielwort))
ddfrq$Zielwort <- factor(rep(levels(df$Zielwort), 2),
                         levels = c('A', 'verb-te', 'B', 'weil', 'er', 'Pr+1', 'Pr+2'))
h <- ggplot(ddfrq, aes(x = Zielwort, y = freq))
h + geom_bar(aes(fill = gp), stat = 'identity') + theme_bw() +
    facet_wrap(~ gp, nrow = 1) +
    scale_fill_manual(breaks = levels(ddfrq$gp), values = c('green','red')) +
    opts(legend.position = 'none') + opts(panel.border = theme_blank()) +
    opts(axis.ticks = theme_blank()) + ylab('Anzahl Fixationen')
ggsave('zeilbars2.pdf', height = 5, width = 7)

The second of these is attached; both worked, both are identical. If this doesn't work on your system, you should check the versions of R, ggplot2 and plyr against mine. I didn't do this test in a fresh session, which is why a bunch of unrelated packages are loaded below.

HTH,
Dennis

parts:
Hi Dennis,

thanks for the suggestions, both work on my system. However, I don't get my original data to work properly so here's a reduced dataset to play with: http://dl.dropbox.com/u/6281903/data.dat. I also changed the bulky "kongruent" and "inkongruent" to "A" and "B". Factorizing dstroi didn't change the output.
The general structure is the following: for every combination of subj, cond, srcroi and dstroi, there's an integer indicating how many fixations that particular dstroi received when the regression came from that srcroi. This is eyetracking data and I'm only interested in regressions from srcroi 5 to 8 to dstroi 1 to 7 (when dstroi >= srcroi, cfc is always 0).

Best,
Paul
